summary.en: Read matrix coordinates and implement addition, multiplication, transposition and diagonal totals.
summary.bn: সারি ও কলাম ধরে ম্যাট্রিক্স পড়ো; যোগ, গুণ, ট্রান্সপোজ ও কর্ণের যোগফল করো।

notes: Fixed rectangular arrays are available in C89; these matrix loops use C99 declarations.

sections.title: Use two coordinates for a table
Addition and multiplication use different rules
Transpose and diagonals have their own bounds
Nested arrays have a stable layout
Let the shape guide the loops

examples.title: Read and print a rectangular matrix
examples.explanationHtml: The input fills row zero before row one. The output prints two rows of three entries.

examples.title: Add two matrices element by element
examples.explanationHtml: Matching coordinates give rows 6 8 and 10 12. Addition never mixes a row with a different column.

examples.title: Multiply a 2 by 3 matrix by a 3 by 2 matrix
examples.explanationHtml: The first result is 1*7 + 2*9 + 3*11 = 58. Each output cell starts at zero before adding three products.

examples.title: Transpose a rectangle into a new shape
examples.explanationHtml: The first row 1 2 3 becomes the first column. A rectangular transpose needs storage with reversed dimensions.

examples.title: Sum two diagonals separately
examples.explanationHtml: Each diagonal totals 15. Their union totals 25 because the central 5 must be counted once.

practice.title: Add equal rectangular matrices
practice.statementHtml: Read rows and columns from 1 to 4, then two matrices of that shape with entries from -10 to 10. Print Shape and entries: before the first input and Second matrix: before the second matrix. Print their sum with one row per line and spaces between entries.
hints: Use the same row and column to access both operands.

practice.title: Print a transpose
practice.statementHtml: Read rows and columns from 1 to 4, then entries from -10 to 10. Print Shape and entries: first. Print the transpose with columns output rows and rows output columns.
hints: Reading a[column][row] in the output loops exchanges the coordinates.

practice.title: Total each matrix row
practice.statementHtml: Read rows and columns from 1 to 4, then entries from -10 to 10. Print Shape and entries: first, then one row sum per line.
hints: Reset the subtotal inside the outer loop.

practice.title: Multiply small square matrices
practice.statementHtml: Read n twice as rows and columns, each equal and from 1 to 4, then two n by n matrices with entries from -10 to 10. Use the prompts Shape and entries: and Second matrix:. Print the product matrix.
hints: A product cell needs a fresh accumulator and a third loop.

practice.title: Diagonal union without double counting
practice.statementHtml: Read an equal row and column count from 1 to 4, then a square matrix with entries from -10 to 10. Print Shape and entries: first, then the sum of entries on either diagonal, counting the center once.
hints: Only add the secondary entry when its column differs from the primary entry.

quiz.explanation: The outer extent counts rows; each row is an array of three ints.

quiz.prompt: Which subscript selects the last element of int a[2][3]?
quiz.explanation: Both dimensions start at zero and have their own bounds.

quiz.prompt: Reading row one, column zero selects which initialized value?
quiz.explanation: The second row begins with four.

quiz.prompt: What shape results from multiplying a 2 by 3 matrix by a 3 by 4 matrix?
quiz.explanation: The shared inner dimension is three, while the outer dimensions determine the result.

quiz.prompt: Which two matrices can be added coordinate by coordinate?
options: Any pair with equal total element counts
Two matrices with equal row and column counts
quiz.explanation: Addition pairs the same row and column, so both dimensions must agree.

quiz.prompt: A two-by-two primary diagonal is totaled. Which sum is printed?
quiz.explanation: The primary diagonal uses two and nine, totaling eleven.

quiz.prompt: What is the transpose shape of a 2 by 5 matrix?
quiz.explanation: Transposition exchanges the coordinate roles and therefore the extents.

quiz.prompt: Why reset the multiplication sum for every result cell?
options: To make the input matrices zero
Each cell is a separate row-column dot product
To avoid reading the left matrix
To reduce all multiplication to addition once
quiz.explanation: Carrying a preceding cell total would add unrelated products to the new cell.

quiz.prompt: The first multiplication cell combines one row and one column. Which dot product result appears?
quiz.explanation: Two times four plus three times five equals twenty-three.

quiz.prompt: In an n by n square, which coordinates form the secondary diagonal?
quiz.explanation: The row increases from zero while the column decreases from n minus one.

quiz.prompt: What must be corrected when adding two diagonal sums into a union total for odd n?
quiz.explanation: Both separate diagonals already include the same center, so their sum counts it twice.

quiz.prompt: Is a[0][3] a legal next-row access for int a[2][3]?
options: No, it exceeds the first row subarray
Yes, every flat offset is legal
quiz.explanation: Contiguous nested layout does not permit indexing beyond an individual row's element range.

keyPoints.en: A two-dimensional array is an array of row arrays.
keyPoints.bn: দ্বিমাত্রিক অ্যারে আসলে সারির অ্যারেগুলোর অ্যারে।

keyPoints.en: C stores complete rows consecutively in row-major order.
keyPoints.bn: C-তে একটি সারির পর পরের সারি মেমরিতে থাকে।
ম্যাট্রিক্স যোগে দুইটির সারি ও কলামসংখ্যা সমান লাগে।

keyPoints.en: Matrix multiplication pairs left columns with right rows.
keyPoints.bn: ম্যাট্রিক্স গুণে বামের কলামসংখ্যা ডানের সারিসংখ্যার সমান লাগে।

keyPoints.en: Transposition exchanges row and column positions.
keyPoints.bn: ট্রান্সপোজ করলে সারি ও কলামের অবস্থান বদলায়।

keyPoints.en: Two diagonals share the center in an odd-sized square.
keyPoints.bn: বিজোড় আকারের বর্গ ম্যাট্রিক্সে দুই কর্ণের কেন্দ্র একই।

examQuestions.question: State the shape rule and cell formula for multiplying A with shape r by k and B with shape k by c.
examQuestions.answerHtml: The shared dimension k must match. The result has r rows and c columns. Cell [i][j] is the sum over t from zero through k minus one of A[i][t] times B[t][j]. Reset that cell sum before its inner loop. The total work is O(r*k*c).

#include <stdio.h>



int main(void)
{
    int a[2][3] = {{1, 2, 3}, {4, 5, 6}};
    printf("%d\n", a[1][0]);
    return 0;
}

4

The second row begins with four.

examQuestions.question: Read an equal row and column count from 1 to 4, then a square matrix with entries from -10 to 10. Print Shape and entries: first, then the sum of entries on either diagonal, counting the center once.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
#include <stdio.h>



int main(void)
{
    int rows, columns;
    int a[4][4];
    puts("Shape and entries:");
    if (scanf("%d%d", &rows, &columns) != 2 || rows < 1 || rows > 4 ||
        columns < 1 || columns > 4) {
        return 1;
    }
    for (int row = 0; row < rows; row++) {
        for (int column = 0; column < columns; column++) {
            if (scanf("%d", &a[row][column]) != 1 ||
                a[row][column] < -10 || a[row][column] > 10) {
                return 1;
            }
        }
    }
    if (rows != columns) {
        return 1;
    }
    int sum = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) {
        sum += a[i][i];
        if (i != rows - 1 - i) {
            sum += a[i][rows - 1 - i];
        }
    }
    printf("%d\n", sum);
    return 0;
}

Only add the secondary entry when its column differs from the primary entry.

For input 1 1 7, the program prints:

Shape and entries:
7

examQuestions.question: Is a[0][3] a legal next-row access for int a[2][3]? Choose and justify: No, it exceeds the first row subarray; Yes, every flat offset is legal; Only if a[1][0] equals zero; Only on a row-major host.
examQuestions.answerHtml: No, it exceeds the first row subarray. Contiguous nested layout does not permit indexing beyond an individual row's element range.
